issues.legal_issue: An executing court must adjudicate claims of third parties resisting delivery of possession under Order XXI Rules 97 to 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure before directing removal of the obstruction.
Whether a transfer attracts the bar under Order XXI Rule 102 of the Code of Civil Procedure depends on when the transfer occurred in relation to the pending suit and may require evidence.
A decree affirmed in proceedings between the decree-holders and judgment-debtors does not, by itself, bar an enquiry into independent claims raised by third parties who were not bound by the decree.

The Supreme Court should ordinarily not entertain a special leave petition directly against an executing court’s order when an available remedy before the High Court has not been pursued, absent exceptional circumstances.
